## Synthesis — read this first

**The checks ran independently, so one overrides another.** The D3-numbers check concluded that "the ridge map does not pay" still holds; it did not know about the ridge-prior experiment, which refutes it. That conclusion came from shrinking the map toward zero. Shrunk toward the identity, on the same pairs and validation splits, the map gives +0.0541 at 100 pairs (zero prior +0.0081) and +0.0649 at all 9,688 (zero prior +0.0574); its W = I arm reproduces arm B at +0.048994 (`d3_ridge_identity_prior_2026-09-28.json`).

**What changed as a result** (commits on `audit-2026-09-18`, 2026-09-28): the identity-prior experiment was committed; `LINEAGE_TRANSFER_2026-09-28.md` carries a supersession banner rather than a rewrite; CLAUDE.md, AUDIT_2026-09-18.md, NEW_DIRECTIONS_2026-09-20.md, TRANSFER_WALL_2026-08-21.md and the indexes were corrected. **Deliberately NOT acted on** (Leo's call, 2026-09-28): rewriting the D3 writeup, and correcting and republishing the 2026-09-14 deck — the deck findings below are the to-do list for that.

I recomputed every number in LINEAGE_TRANSFER_2026-09-28.md and in the messages of commits 5c1fa95, daf4502 and 3fe971a. I worked from the six D3 artifacts, the home-model per-benchmark artifacts (em_rescore_pooled_probe_2026-09-18.json and head_final_stack_PVFIXED_2026-09-13.json) and the raw QoQ and MedGemma sampled-pool checkpoints. All the arithmetic holds. The pair-1 reference values, both 8-cell macros, every difference, the pair-efficiency curve, the reproducibility deviation, the per-cell table, the +0.0739 native value, the row counts and the stop-token figures match their sources. The stop-token figures and MedGemma's 100% also reproduce exactly from the raw ckpt files. The problems are in interpretation and in which values are compared. (1) The claim that the gain lands 'exactly where the probe already had selection skill on its home model' is contradicted by the home model's own per-benchmark numbers. PathVQA had significant home skill (+0.0567) and transferred nothing, and RadImageNet had the third-highest home skill but is left out of the list. Transfer ranks much closer to the target model's own native gains than to home skill. (2) The pair-1 RIDGE value (+0.0574) comes from a different implementation than pair 2's RIDGE. (4) Only pair 2 is a fine-tune target, yet the 'Claim this' text says 'other fine-tunes... replicated on two pairs'. (5) The two native ceilings differ in training-data sources, not only in volume. The transfer fractions the doc lacks are pair 1 A/B/RIDGE = 55.0%/59.7%/70.0% of native (73.5% with the pilot's RIDGE) and pair 2 = 57.6%/69.1%/76.3%.

**Finding.** The two native ceilings are NOT 'matched to each other in recipe but not in training volume'. Cross-pair comparisons of transfer fractions (G2) are confounded by this.

### B1 · low · CONFIRMED

**Finding.** 'Below ~3,000 pairs the learned map is actively harmful / worse than doing nothing' is true on all three measured points (100, 300 and 1,000 pairs are below zero-shot A for every seed). The crossover with A lies somewhere between 1,000 and 3,000 and was not measured. The column is headed 'vs. free re-standardisation' (B), yet the 'worse than doing nothing' label is computed against A (d3_writeup.py:126), so the column mixes two baselines. 'Pairs fitted' is also a mislabel: both scripts hold out 10% for lambda selection and fit on 90% (for example 8,720 of 9,688). The map never falls below greedy: +0.0081 at 100 pairs.

**Evidence.** d3_pair_efficiency curve.<n>.macro_mean / macro_per_seed: 100 → 0.008107 (seeds 0.0110/0.0090/0.0043); 300 → 0.027184; 1000 → 0.042154 (seeds 0.04472/0.04090/0.04085); 3000 → 0.049266 (sd 0.00376, seeds 0.0532/0.0488/0.0458); all → 0.057414 (1 fit). Versus B = 0.048994: −0.0409, −0.0218, −0.0068, +0.0003, +0.0084. mean and sd recompute exactly from macro_per_seed. d3_pair_efficiency.py fit_map: k = len//10 held for validation, solve on tr only.

**Verifier.** At d3_writeup.py the verdict label is computed as `'worse than doing nothing' if v['macro_mean'] < R['zero_shot_A']`, i.e. against A. The column header says 'vs. free re-standardisation' (B), and the numeric cells are d = macro - B. So the column mixes two baselines. The curve values recompute exactly. Against A: 100 → -0.0370, 300 → -0.0179, 1000 → -0.0029, 3000 → +0.0042. The 1000-pair deficit (-0.0029) equals the pilot-vs-refit deviation (-0.00289), and the best 1000-pair seed (0.04472) is within 0.0004 of A. fit_map holds out k=len//10 for lambda selection and solves on the rest, so 'pairs fitted' really means pairs collected, 90% of them fitted. The directional claim holds on point estimates; this is wording and labelling. — *curve 100 0.008107, 300 0.027184, 1000 0.042154 (seeds 0.04472/0.04090/0.04085), 3000 0.049266, all 0.057414; A 0.045101; B 0.048994; d3_pair_efficiency.py:120 'k = max(1, len(Zq) // 10); va, tr = perm[:k], perm[k:]'*

## D3 — methodology and leakage

I found no leakage. I rebuilt the frozen probes' training set from freeze_pooled_selector.py and got exactly 112,770 rows with 59 dropped, as recipe.json records. Zero img_md5 values overlap between that training set and the held-out rows of Qwen or QoQ in any of the 8 cells. The split key, the standardisers, the choice of ridge strength, the pairing, the greedy baseline, the bootstrap maths and the tie handling are all sound. A read-only re-run of the D3 logic gave the recorded macros exactly: Qwen A/B/RIDGE +0.04510/+0.04899/+0.06030 and QoQ +0.04261/+0.05112/+0.05643. The problems are with what the results are said to show. (1) QoQ's language-model weights sit within about 0.11% of Qwen2.5-VL-7B's, so pair 2 is nearly a repeat of pair 1, not an independent sibling. (2) The pair-efficiency finding that the map is 'worse than doing nothing' comes from how the ridge is set up: it shrinks towards zero, and with fewer than about 3,983 pairs the map cannot reach full rank. At 100 pairs it discards 59% of each held-out state. (3) The two pairs' RIDGE numbers came from different fitting procedures, and simply redrawing the random 90% of pairs used for fitting moves pair 1 by 0.0029. (4) The two step-ups the conclusions depend on (B over A, RIDGE over B) were never given confidence intervals. Once computed, B over A is not significant on pair 1, and RIDGE over B is significant on pair 1 but not on pair 2. (5) RIDGE's gain over B is almost entirely OmniMedVQA, which also supplies 41–43% of the pairs. (6) Everything is in judge currency only, although CLAUDE.md requires exact-match numbers alongside for verifier comparisons.

### P1 · high · CONFIRMED

### P2 · high · CONFIRMED

**Finding.** The claim that the map is 'actively harmful below ~3,000 pairs' comes from the estimator, not from lineage alignment. The ridge shrinks W towards zero, so its output always lies in the span of the training Lingshu vectors, and its rank is at most 0.9n. It cannot be full rank until n is at least about 3,983 (0.9n >= 3584). The crossover near 3,000 pairs matches that bound. The strength is also chosen by mean squared error, which prefers the collapsed map even when its ranking is far worse. An identity prior would fall back to arm B as n goes to 0.

**Evidence.** From my re-run of d3_pair_efficiency seed 0, which reproduces the artifact's per-seed macros exactly (+0.01095 at n=100, +0.05325 at n=3000). At n=100 (layer 20): lambda 1000, rank(W) = 90 with 90 training pairs; the span of those pairs keeps only 0.4128 of held-out state energy; mean ||zW||/||z|| is 0.5030. Validation MSE: mapped 0.6028 < identity 0.9152 < zero map 1.2071, so the criterion picks the collapsed map, yet macro is +0.0110 against B's +0.0490. At n=3000: 0.9611 of energy kept, ratio 0.7864, macro +0.05325. With all pairs, mapped states are still under-dispersed (per-dimension sd 0.8356 vs about 1.0 for the probes' inputs). The recorded curve[*].ridge_lambda is 1000 for every layer and seed except 100 at n=1000 seed 1 and n=3000 seed 1 layer 22. At n=100, lambda is chosen on only 10 validation pairs (d3_pair_efficiency.py:120). The doc's 'actively harmful / not fixable' wording is at lines 65 and 75-78; line 76 measures 'doing nothing' against A (+0.0451) while the table column uses B.

**Verifier.** This is now settled by experiment, not just reasoning. The identity-prior run has landed: results/cascade_methods/artifacts/d3_ridge_identity_prior_2026-09-28.json, COMPLETE=True, prior 'W = I + Delta, ridge penalty on Delta'. Its identity arm reproduces B at +0.0490. With the same subsamples and splits, the curve is 100=+0.0541, 300=+0.0569, 1000=+0.0598, 3000=+0.0574, all=+0.0649. The zero-prior curve behind the doc is 100=+0.0081, 300=+0.0272, 1000=+0.0422, 3000=+0.0493, all=+0.0574. So 'worse than doing nothing below ~3,000 pairs' and 'not fixable by collecting fewer pairs' are artefacts of shrinking toward zero. With an identity prior, the map beats B at every n. At all pairs it beats B by about +0.0159 instead of +0.0084, which also undermines 'the ridge map should be reported as a measured negative'. The validation-MSE diagnostic agrees with the finder: at n=100, seed 0, layer 20, identity MSE on the same split is 0.9152. The inconsistent baseline is also confirmed. d3_writeup.py:126 labels a row 'worse than doing nothing' when it is below R['zero_shot_A'] (A), while the column is headed 'vs. free re-standardisation' (B). Line 131 prints A (+0.0451) as 'doing nothing'. The rank bound (rank(W) <= 0.9n, so full rank needs n >= 3983) is correct algebra; the experiment makes it moot. Severity is high because a headline conclusion in the writeup is refuted by an artifact that already exists. — *d3_ridge_identity_prior_2026-09-28.json VERDICT: 'Identity-prior curve: 100=+0.0541, 300=+0.0569, 1000=+0.0598, 3000=+0.0574, all=+0.0649. Zero-prior curve (d3_pair_efficiency_2026-09-21.json): 100=+0.0081, 300=+0.0272, 1000=+0.0422, 3000=+0.0493, all=+0.0574.'; vs_zero_prior.rows['100'].identity_minus_zero_prior = 0.04597; d3_writeup.py:126 'if v["macro_mean"] < R["zero_shot_A"]'*

**Fix.** Until the identity-prior run lands, limit the claim to 'a ridge map shrunk towards zero'. Fit the map as W = I + Delta with the penalty on Delta, or choose strength with identity (lambda to infinity) as one of the options. Choose the strength with a ranking-aware criterion (for example rank agreement of probe scores on paired rows), not MSE alone. Use B consistently as the 'doing nothing' baseline.

### P10 · low · PLAUSIBLE

**Finding.** The leakage guard only catches exact pixel duplicates (md5 of decoded RGB). Exact duplicates between splits do exist, so near-duplicates (resized or re-encoded copies) are plausible and have not been checked.

But 'near-duplicates: not measured' is factually wrong. The audit sweep src/audit_2026_09_18/sweeps/data-integrity/05_crossbench_overlap.py ran a 64-bit dHash check. Its log (/data/dan/audit_2026-09-18/tmp/data-integrity/out/05_crossbench_overlap.log) reports dHash-only matches from the four training domains into the held-out union that the md5 guard misses: kvasir_open 5, pathvqa_open_train 7, slake_open_train 100, vqa_rad_open_train 12 (124 total). What would settle it: a visual or thumbnail-distance check of those 124. *Location:* `/home/jamesyang/medvlthinker-imgdiff-compute/.claude/worktrees/audit-2026-09-18/src/training_methods/extract_generator_hidden.py:71-75`

**Checked and holds:**

- Q1: the frozen probes were trained only on the training half plus the original four domains, with held-out images removed. Evaluation uses only held-out rows. The empirical overlap is 0.
- Q2: no image can land on both sides of the split. The split depends on img_md5 alone, so every question on a given image, in any benchmark, falls in the same half. The shared SLAKE/VQA-RAD cache is filtered by benchmark.
- Q3: the arm-B standardiser, the ridge-input standardiser, the choice of ridge strength and the pairing use only training-half states and no labels.
- Q4: the greedy baseline is the target model's own temperature-0 answer, scored by the same judge on the same held-out questions. The skip for questions missing from the judge dict never fires, so it cannot treat the arms differently.
- Q5: the boot() maths is correct. It sums differences per image, resamples images with replacement, and takes the ratio of summed differences to summed question counts. The point estimate is the per-question mean, and the percentile interval is the standard cluster bootstrap for a mean over clusters of unequal size. Caveats: slake (49 held-out images) and vqa_rad (58) are small enough that coverage may fall short, and the artifacts give no macro-level CI (see P4).
- Q6: ties in the rank_avg + argmax readout are rare and do not shift the arms materially. Row order matters only through ties. First-index tie-breaking does not hide a boost, because the first row is not better than a random pick.
- Q7: within each pair, A, B and RIDGE are compared on identical questions, candidate pools, greedy labels and the same 24 frozen heads; only the input transform differs. My re-run reproduced every recorded macro exactly.
- The zero-shot transfer is real selection skill, not something the candidate pool gives for free. Label-free baselines on the same held-out questions score below greedy.
- Q9 (lineage and setup): QoQ is qwen2_5_vl with hidden size 3584 and 28 layers, and its card names Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct as the base. Lingshu's weights are close to Qwen's, which fits a fine-tune, although Lingshu's local README carries no base_model tag. All three caches were extracted with the same system prompt, the same max_pixels and no adapter.


## D3 — the identity-prior ridge experiment

I ran the experiment and it refutes the D3 writeup's pair-efficiency claim. The failure at small n comes from shrinking the map toward zero, not from the alignment map itself. I added one new script, /home/jamesyang/medvlthinker-imgdiff-compute/.claude/worktrees/audit-2026-09-18/src/audit_2026_09_18/d3_ridge_identity_prior.py. A diff against d3_pair_efficiency.py shows only the requested changes: a residual ridge with W = I + Delta, 1e6 and 1e7 added to the lambda grid, an explicit identity arm, and a vs_zero_prior block. It wrote results/cascade_methods/artifacts/d3_ridge_identity_prior_2026-09-28.json (COMPLETE true, 1760.6 s, 4 threads, no crash). The identity arm matches arm B exactly: +0.04899402078777673, the same value as the pilot. Shrinking toward the identity puts the map ABOVE arm B at every n: 100 pairs +0.0541, 300 +0.0569, 1000 +0.0598, 3000 +0.0574, all 9,688 pairs +0.0649. The zero-prior curve was +0.0081, +0.0272, +0.0422, +0.0493, +0.0574. All 13 paired seed comparisons favour the identity prior. So "worse than doing nothing below ~3,000 pairs", "not fixable by collecting fewer pairs" and "B to RIDGE is worth only +0.0084" all describe the zero-prior estimator, not label-free alignment. One part of the hypothesis did not hold: the label-free selector never shrank all the way to W = I. It picked lambda = 1000 in 38 of 39 fits. The result is judge-only, has no question-level paired CI, and the full-data point is a single seed. The QoQ pair was not re-run.

**Finding.** The writeup says the ridge map is 'worse than doing nothing' and 'actively harmful' below ~3,000 pairs. That is an artifact of shrinking toward zero. With identity shrinkage the map beats arm A (+0.0451) and arm B (+0.0490) at every n and on every seed. At 100 pairs it scores +0.0541 against +0.0081 for the zero-prior map.

Paired identity-minus-zero per seed (vs_zero_prior.rows.*.identity_minus_zero_prior_per_seed): 100 [0.04366, 0.04623, 0.04802]; 300 [0.02864, 0.02948, 0.03112]; 1000 [0.01423, 0.02142, 0.01738]; 3000 [0.00394, 0.01031, 0.01029]; all [0.00749].

### B5 · low · CONFIRMED

**Finding.** In d3_finish.sh (set -u without -e), the verdict-repair python block has no error check, and it rewrites the only copy of the then-untracked artifact in place. If that block raised (e.g. a KeyError), the script would still log 'verdict repaired', regenerate the doc and commit the unrepaired max(macro) VERDICT under a commit message saying it was repaired. json.dump(a, open(p,"w")) truncates before writing, so a failure part-way through the dump would destroy the 2.5-hour fit output. The writeup step would then crash and nothing would be committed, but the data would be gone. Likewise `> "$DOC"` truncates the tracked doc before the generator runs, and git add is unchecked.

**Evidence.** d3_finish.sh:5 `set -u`; :39 `python3 - "$ART" << 'PY'` with no `|| {...}` (compare :27, which has one); :57 json.dump(a,open(p,"w"),indent=1); :60 unconditional `say "verdict repaired"`; :62 `python3 ... d3_writeup.py > "$DOC"`; :66 `git add` unchecked. The artifact was first added to git in 3fe971a (`git log -- ...head_final_stack_qoq...` shows only 3fe971a), so the repair ran on an untracked sole copy.

**Verifier.** The mechanism is real. set -u has no -e. The repair heredoc at :39 has no '|| {...}' guard, unlike the validation block at :27. The next line (:60, say "verdict repaired") is unconditional. json.dump(a, open(p,"w")) truncates the file before writing. `> "$DOC"` truncates the doc before the generator runs. git add is unchecked. The artifact was untracked until 3fe971a (git log -- artifact lists only 3fe971a), so the repair rewrote the sole copy in place. It did not trigger: d3_finish.nohup shows 'validated' and 'verdict repaired: shipped arm pooled_ens: +0.0739 ...', and the stored VERDICT/shipped_arm/best_arm_posthoc/verdict_repaired_note are present. The artifact's macro values (0.06957/0.07392/0.07091) and per-cell values match the MACRO and per-cell lines in stack_qoq.log. This is a latent risk in a one-shot script that has already succeeded, so low. — *d3_finish.sh:5 'set -u'; :27 '... << 'PY' || { echo "FAILED: artifact did not validate ...' vs :39 'python3 - "$ART" << 'PY'' (no guard); :57 json.dump(a,open(p,"w"),indent=1); :60 say "verdict repaired"; :62 python3 ... d3_writeup.py > "$DOC"; :66 git add "$ART" "$DOC" (unchecked). `git log --format=%h -- .../head_final_stack_qoq_2026-09-28.json` -> 3fe971a only.*

**Fix.** Use `set -euo pipefail` or add `|| { echo FAILED... > "$MARK"; exit 1; }` to every step. Copy the artifact to a .bak first, then write to a temp file and os.replace it. Generate the doc into a temp file and mv it only on success.

*Location:* `src/audit_2026_09_18/d3_finish.sh:5,39-60,62,66`

### B6 · low · CONFIRMED

**Finding.** d3_finish.sh's completeness check and commit are loose. (a) `grep -q "n/a"` only logs a warning and never blocks the commit, while the hard-coded commit message asserts 'Fills the one value left open' and quotes 87,308 / 145,085 / 5-seed without reading them from the artifact. (b) `git add A B; git commit` has no pathspec, so anything already staged in the worktree index would be swept into the commit. (c) The wait uses the broad `pgrep -f "head_final_stack.py --generator qoq"`: it matches any shell or grep whose command line contains that text (keeping it waiting up to the 3 h cap), and misses the fit if the arguments are reordered. (d) Nothing stops two copies running at once, and the log shows two starts 18 s apart. Had both reached the commit step, they would have raced on the doc's `>` truncation, and the second's empty commit would have overwritten the DONE marker with FAILED. This time the outcome was correct: 3fe971a touches exactly the two intended files, and the numbers in the message match the artifact.

**Evidence.** d3_finish.sh:63 `grep -q "n/a" "$DOC" && say "WARNING..."`; :66-86 add+commit with no pathspec and a fixed message; :17 pgrep -f pattern; logs/d3_finish.log: '[04:13:09] watching for ...' and '[04:13:27] watching for ...', then a single validated/repaired/committed sequence at 04:19:08. `git show --stat 3fe971a` shows 2 files: head_final_stack_qoq (118+) and LINEAGE_TRANSFER (8 +/-5).

**Verifier.** (a) `grep -q "n/a"` only logs (:63), and the commit message is a fixed heredoc with hard-coded 87,308 / 145,085 / 5-seed. (b) `git add` + `git commit` has no pathspec, so anything already staged would be swept in. (c) The wait uses `pgrep -f "head_final_stack.py --generator qoq"`. pgrep excludes itself, but any other process whose command line contains that text would keep the loop alive, and reordered arguments would be missed. (d) There is no lock, and d3_finish.log shows two 'watching' starts (04:13:09 and 04:13:27) but only one validated/repaired/committed sequence, and d3_finish.nohup shows one validation. This run turned out correctly: 3fe971a touches exactly 2 files (the artifact with 118 insertions and the doc with 8 +/-5), the doc now has 0 'n/a' or 'not on disk' matches, and 87,308 / 145,085 / 5 seeds match the artifacts. These are code-hygiene risks for next time only. — *d3_finish.sh:17 pgrep -f "head_final_stack.py --generator qoq"; :63 grep -q "n/a" "$DOC" && say "WARNING..."; :66-67 git add ...; git commit -q -F -; logs/d3_finish.log '[04:13:09] watching for ...' '[04:13:27] watching for ...' then a single '[04:19:08] committed: 3fe971a'; `git show --stat 3fe971a` -> '2 files changed, 121 insertions(+), 5 deletions(-)'; `grep -c "n/a\|not on disk" LINEAGE_TRANSFER_2026-09-28.md` -> 0.*

**Fix.** Validate the specific value, e.g. python -c that d3_lineage_qoq macro or head_final_stack_qoq macro.pooled_ens is finite and that the doc table row is not n/a, and exit non-zero on failure. Use `git commit -- "$ART" "$DOC"`, or check that `git diff --cached --name-only` is exactly those two. Wait on the fit's PID (`tail --pid=$PID -f /dev/null`, or kill -0 in a loop) rather than pgrep -f. Wrap the whole script in `flock -n logs/.d3_finish.lock`. Build the commit message numbers from the artifact.

I checked all 11 claim groups against the source artifacts in both artifact trees, ckpts/ and feats_hidden/, and recomputed several values: oracle@8/@32 from the meta labels, the probe parameter count from the 24 state dicts plus the 3 standardizer files, MedGemma |h_span| and |h_last| per layer from 3 float32 caches, and the LoRA-SFT and 7B-vs-32B tallies. Almost every number matches its source to the stated precision: 2.62% / +0.0061, 1.99/2.95 and 2.74/3.59, +0.1215→+0.1932, +0.0044, +0.0737 [+0.0608,+0.0864], +0.0679, +0.0047 [−0.0077,+0.0171], +0.0156, +0.057/+0.066, +0.0814, +0.0276, +0.0412, +0.0573 [+0.0483,+0.0663], 0.0033, 22,053,912 / 88.2 MB, 100% / 58.5%, and +0.0142. In judge currency the same table gives 1 loss, 2 ties, 1 win, and CLAUDE.md §0a:223-224 states it with no currency. Apart from (a), I found no other place where §0a contradicts an artifact.

**Finding.** '1.7% of extra coverage converted' mislabels the metric. converted_pct is (verifier−greedy)/(oracle−greedy) at N=32, i.e. a share of the TOTAL headroom above greedy. Measured against the EXTRA coverage bought going 8→32, vqamed converts about 5.2%.

**Evidence.** budget_conversion_sc32_2026-09-17.json vqamed_open.32: verifier_minus_greedy 0.0044 / headroom_above_greedy 0.2562 = 1.7%. Extra coverage: oracle 0.1987→0.3475 (+0.1488) vs verifier 0.0880→0.0957 (+0.0077), so 0.0077/0.1488 = 5.2%.

**Verifier.** converted_pct is computed as (verifier − greedy) / (oracle − greedy) at N=32, which gives 0.0044/0.2562 = 1.7%. That is a share of the total headroom above greedy. Against the extra coverage bought going from 8 to 32 samples, the share is (0.0957−0.0880)/(0.3475−0.1987) = 0.0077/0.1488 = 5.2%. The artifact's own VERDICT string contains the same mislabel ('oracle rises +0.1488 ... and the probe converts 1.7% of it'), so the session claim inherited it from the artifact. The qualitative conclusion, that the probe converts almost none of it, holds either way. — *cells.vqamed_open.32: verifier_minus_greedy 0.0044, headroom_above_greedy 0.2562, converted_pct 1.7; .8.oracle 0.1987, .32.oracle 0.3475, .8.verifier 0.088, .32.verifier 0.0957; VERDICT '...oracle rises +0.1488 over the same range and the probe converts 1.7% of it'*

**Fix.** Say '1.7% of the headroom above greedy at N=32'. If the claim is about new coverage, quote ~5% instead.

### C9 · low · CONFIRMED

**Finding.** 'MedGemma float16 overflow: max |h_span| 58,240 vs 65,504 on layer 27' is not an artifact number. It comes from a code comment measured on 8 SLAKE rows. On the full float32 caches, h_span NEVER exceeds 65,504 on any layer (layer-27 max 58,933-59,776, zero rows over the ceiling). The overflow actually occurs in h_last, which the probe does not read. So 'h_span overflow' is wrong; the float32 switch is still justified, by h_last and by the ~9% headroom.

**Evidence.** src/training_methods/extract_generator_hidden.py:384-385 comment '36,480 at layer 18 to 58,240 at layer 27' (8 SLAKE rows). My recompute of max|h_span| at L27: generator_eval_medgemma_slake_open.npz 58932.7, vqa_rad_open 59457.3, radimagenet_open 59776.0; rows>65504 = 0; nonfinite = 0. h_last L27: slake max 72704.0 with 3 rows >65504; vqa_rad 64000.0.

**Verifier.** I recomputed per-row max |value| from the float32 MedGemma-4B caches, with meta model google--medgemma-4b-it. h_span never exceeds 65,504 on any layer. At L27 its maximum is 58,932.7 on SLAKE, 59,457.3 on VQA-RAD and 59,776.0 on RadImageNet, with 0 rows over the ceiling and 0 non-finite values. h_last at L27 does exceed it: 72,704 with 3 rows over on SLAKE, and 71,680 with 11 rows over on RadImageNet. The 58,240 figure comes only from the code comment at extract_generator_hidden.py:384-385, measured on 8 SLAKE rows. That comment implies h_span rows would have overflowed; in fact the overflow is in h_last. The float32 decision is still correct, and no downstream number changes. That makes this a wording and provenance error; I downgraded severity to low. — *slake_open h_span 27 max 58932.70703125 rows>65504 0; vqa_rad_open h_span 27 max 59457.2578125 rows>65504 0; radimagenet_open h_span 27 max 59776.0 rows>65504 0; h_last 27 slake max 72704.0 rows>65504 3; radimagenet 71680.0 rows>65504 11; extract_generator_hidden.py:384 'max |h_span| runs 36,480 at layer 18 to 58,240 at layer 27'*

**Fix.** Restate: 'h_span peaks at ~59.8k on L27 (below the fp16 ceiling); h_last reaches 72.7k and does overflow fp16'. Cite the caches, not the comment.

## The 2026-09-14 professor deck

I extracted every number from both copies of the deck and traced each one to its artifact. The published artifact (https://claude.ai/artifact/BZ9E9ts1bA3vPJ4J16By4p, updated 2026-09-14) matches the uncorrected main copy almost exactly: only 2 lines differ, against 111 for the worktree copy. The 2026-09-20 corrections exist only on the unmerged audit-2026-09-18 branch, so the professor is still looking at the uncorrected deck. 201 of the values match their sources exactly, but many of them describe a different model, benchmark population or currency from the one the slide claims. The most serious problems are: (1) the "today" cost row is the artifact's hypothetical FREE capture path; the path actually run costs 14.90x, against 15.18x for the LoRA. I also found errors in the worktree's own correction notes: several numbers it calls unsourced are sourced, its +0.1098 recomputation does not hold, and it reads a normalised 0.51 as "the random floor". I edited nothing and republished nothing; scratch files are only in /tmp (deck_main.txt, deck_wt.txt, deckaudit_leaves.pkl, deckaudit_find.py).
